checklist_items.22.1: covered: every entry the shell actually renders in the sider is enumerated at runtime (19 of them, read from .app-sider .app-nav rather than from a route table) and each is entered by deep link in both en and zh. For each entry the case asserts the address it settles on, that exactly one menu entry is selected, that the selected entry is that same entry, and that a non-empty page title is rendered; then it calls page.reload() and re-asserts the same address, the same selected entry and the same title, so the position is proven to survive a refresh rather than only on entry. A child route is accepted only where the product itself redirects: /analytics settles on /analytics/usage (AnalyticsPage.tsx:98) and the address is read after the page renders, so the pre-redirect address is never mistaken for the landing one. The deployments surface is covered in its own right: /deployments keeps selected=Deployments with title Deployments, and /deployments?deployment=<id> rebuilds the same title, the same highlight and the same drawer title after a reload.
checklist_items.22.2: covered for the deployments surface, which owns a URL parameter of its own: the list keeps its open detail in the address (?deployment=<id>, DeploymentsPage.tsx:130), so the address, the highlighted menu entry and the page title are three independent witnesses that must agree. Two entries are visited by clicking the menu, then page.go_back() and page.go_forward() each assert all three together - address, selected entry and title - so a restored address with a stale highlight or title fails. The ?deployment=<id> deep link opens the drawer with the matching title and leaves the highlight unchanged; page.reload() keeps the parameter, the drawer and the same drawer title; Escape clears the parameter while the address, the highlight and the title still agree. Entries are addressed by their menu key rather than their label, because the label is translated and this case runs in both languages.
checklist_items.22.3: covered for the single role this build can create, with the administrator-only branch recorded and deliberately not claimed. User.Role has exactly one write point and it hardcodes admin (internal/server/store/auth.go:31), so no product path creates a second role and an admin-versus-user comparison cannot be built from two real identities. What is asserted: the session's own role read from /api/v1/auth/me is admin; all 19 sider entries are rendered for it; and a direct call to GET /api/v1/deployments made outside the page's own requests, carrying only the session cookie, answers 200 with an items/total list. The 403 ErrorAdministratorRequired branch at internal/server/api/auth.go:240 does exist and is recorded as existing, but reaching it needs signed claims carrying a non-admin role, which requires the master key; a forged token would be neither a real user path nor honest evidence, so it is not claimed. GPUWorks does not use the Router organization/IAM model: there is no organization scope, role-assignment UI or per-resource IAM policy to enumerate.
checklist_items.22.4: covered by making a real session expire under real polling. The cookie cannot witness this: the product writes it with the session's absolute deadline on login and on renewal alike (internal/server/api/auth.go:76 and :219 both pass AbsoluteExpiresAt), so its expiry never reflects idle renewal - an earlier attempt compared that value and its own positive control rejected it as sub-second float jitter. Instead a second isolated server runs the product's own session_idle_timeout key at 3s; the session performs real GET polls of /api/v1/auth/me for 6.8s, twice the deadline. The first 7 polls answer 200 and the last 9 answer 401, with the first 401 at 3.17s, so the session expired on schedule while being polled: a passive poll is not human activity and cannot renew it. This matches the product rule that renewal sits in a branch that skips GET/HEAD/OPTIONS (api/auth.go:213-219). The second server is stopped in a finally block.
checklist_items.22.5: covered for the navigation, the first screen, the table's live text and the not-found surface, in en and in zh in the same contract (two full runs). Expectations are read from the shipped locale files rather than copied, so they are the product's own wording. In each language the case asserts that the locale's own navigation label for deployments is rendered and that the other language's label is not; that the page title equals the locale's deployments page title and is not the other language's; and that every table column header is translated text, with an explicit rejection of any header that looks like an internal field name (snake_case, or camelCase starting lowercase). The not-found page's own title and description are asserted in the same locale.
checklist_items.22.6: covered by real keyboard operation and computed style, on the deployments list while the deployment still exists (its disabled controls derive from the running state, DeploymentsPage.tsx:243-244, so a deleted deployment would leave nothing to read). focus-visible is reached the way a keyboard user reaches it: body is clicked to reset focus and Tab is pressed 14 times, and for each landed element getComputedStyle is read; 4 of them painted a real outline and the measured widths were 2px and 3px, so the ring is a painted outline of measurable width rather than a zero-width placeholder or a focus() call that would not prove keyboard reachability. Colour and disabled state come from the browser too: the 4 controls rendered as disabled were each confirmed genuinely disabled by attribute or aria, and the selected entry's computed colour (rgb(0, 91, 212)) was read again after a reload and found unchanged, which is a theme value rather than a one-off literal.
checklist_items.22.7: covered for the SPA fallback and the error surface, which is where this item bites: an address that has no route is answered directly with 200 and content-type text/html, so the status alone cannot distinguish a real page from one that has no route. The case records that 200, then loads the address in the browser and asserts that the app rendered its own not-found title, its own description, and the exact address it was given - so a wrong or dead deep link cannot hide behind the fallback. It also asserts that no sider entry is highlighted, since a highlight would claim the page exists, and that the not-found page's own recovery action reaches a real deployments page with a rendered title. The link targets are taken from the locale files, so the same assertions hold in en and zh.
